methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $690M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)

data.narrative:
Bethlehem Steel Corp is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $690M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine private peers (including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics) and one public comparable (277810.KQ), though the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage matches for reliable median-based triangulation.

Given data constraints, Stage-Progression methodology is the primary applicable approach. Using the $690M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-stage advancement, this method implies a valuation of $828M. A sensitivity range accounting for stage-typical variance yields a low of $704M and a high of $952M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $704M to $952M, with $828M as the central estimate. Key uncertainties stem from limited same-stage peer comparables in the robotics and manufacturing sector, which constrains validation through peer-median methods. Future refinement would benefit from narrower peer identification or disclosure of revenue and growth metrics to enable revenue multiple or DCF-based approaches.
